title: Optional Coverage Add-Ons Premium Billing Rules
content:
Rider premium for the Optional Coverage Add-Ons is billed alongside the base contract and posted to the rider's own premium balance.

## Clauses in force

1. **Monthly-billed base.** On a monthly-billed base, the rider's monthly rider premium is billed with each base installment from the first base billing period that starts on or after the add date. A rider added on the base enrollment date is billed from the first installment.
2. **Real estate base.** A rider on a real estate contract is billed as annual-billed for each 12-month buyer contract year.
3. **Payments.** Payments are applied to the rider's own balance.
4. **No portfolio discount.** A rider premium is never discounted by a landlord portfolio discount.
5. **Open riders only.** Rider premium is billed only while the rider status is waiting period or active. The rider's status is read from Bridgewell's records of that rider before a premium is billed.
6. **Suspended base.** When the base contract is suspended for nonpayment, rider requests are not accepted either.

## Retired clause, in part

The clause that, on an annual-billed base, one prorated annual rider premium is billed on the add date (or on each renewal term start), equal to the monthly rider premium times 12 reduced by the annual pay discount rate, multiplied by the rider's term days and divided by the number of days in the base term, rounded to the cent, is **no longer in force** as the amount due for a rider on a homeowner or rental property service contract; for such a rider the amount due on that premium is now its corrected term premium, under the current basis.

What the clause still governs:

- On an annual-billed base one prorated annual rider premium is still billed on the add date or on each renewal term start.
- A rider on a real estate contract is still billed as annual-billed for each 12-month buyer contract year at the amount the clause states: the monthly rider premium times 12 reduced by the annual pay discount rate, multiplied by the days from the later of its term start date and add date through its term end date, both days counted, divided by the number of days in its base term, and rounded to the cent.

The rate figures themselves (the monthly rider premium and the annual pay discount rate of each rider) remain the published figures.

## Monthly billing start (hypothetical dates)

| Add date | Base billing periods start on | First period billed for the rider |
|---|---|---|
| The base enrollment date | The enrollment date | The first installment |
| 10 May | The 1st of each month | The period starting 1 June |
| 1 June | The 1st of each month | The period starting 1 June |

## Real estate buyer-year premium (hypothetical inputs)

A Bridgewell Well Pump Rider (USD 8.99 a month, annual pay discount rate 0.10) on a real estate contract whose 365-day buyer contract year starts on the closing date, the rider having been added before closing: 8.99 times 12 is 107.88; reduced by 0.10 it is 97.092; multiplied by 365 and divided by 365, and rounded to the cent, the premium is USD 97.09.

## Points of judgement

**A rider was removed. Is premium still billed for it?** No. Premium is billed only while the rider status is waiting period or active.

**A landlord holds a portfolio discount on rental contracts. Does it reduce the rider premium?** No. A rider premium is never discounted by a landlord portfolio discount.

superseded_clauses: On an annual-billed base, one prorated annual rider premium is billed on added_date (or on each renewal term start), equal to monthly_rider_premium times 12 reduced by annual_pay_discount_rate, multiplied by addon_msr_rider_term_days and divided by the number of days in the base term, rounded to the cent.
